family.name: Business Analyst
family.summary: Three senior stakeholders want things that can’t all be true: spot the conflict hiding in their numbers, propose a design they can agree on, and fix requirements that no one could test.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where do the requirements clash?
stages.summary: Find the conflict hidden in three stakeholders' numbers (demand far above manual capacity) and the questions to ask. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your proposal
stages.summary: Propose a design all three can sign. Tests trade-offs and quantifying them. Think aloud.

stages.title: The sign-off meeting
stages.summary: A stakeholder pushes back on their proposal. Tests facilitation and adapting.

stages.title: Review the draft requirements
stages.summary: Requirements that are vague, untestable and contradict each other. Think aloud.

stages.title: User stories (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write user stories with acceptance criteria using AI. Catches untestable criteria and invented requirements.

stages.title: Stakeholders who disagreed
stages.summary: A real time they brought conflicting stakeholders to a decision. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the business analyst on a project at **Setu Supplies** to rebuild how new supplier registrations are handled. Today it's mostly email and spreadsheets. Three people must sign off the requirements.

items: **Head of Sales:** "Every registration must get a decision within 24 hours. Competitors do it in 6 hours. This is non-negotiable."
**Head of Risk:** "Every registration needs three manual checks: identity, documents and a phone call. No exceptions. Last year fraud cost us 0.6% of value."
**Head of Operations:** "My team of 6 can do about 15 full checks each a day. We're not getting more people this year."

brief.caption: From last month’s data
rows: New new supplier registrations per working day
Of those, share with no issues found in any check

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: What makes a requirement good, in your view?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Can all three requirements be met? Show why or why not with the numbers.** Then list the three questions you would ask before writing any requirements.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Route by risk: automatic checks for small, clean cases; manual checks for the rest
Keep every check manual and ask for more operations staff
Keep every check and change the promise from 24 to 72 hours
Launch for one city first and decide later

prompt.text: **What do you propose?** Pick one, show with numbers whether it fits the capacity, and say what each stakeholder gives up.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Route by risk: automatic checks for small, clean cases; manual checks for the rest"

prompt.text: The Head of Risk says: "Automatic checks are how fraudsters get in. I won't sign unless every registration gets a phone call." The Head of Sales says: "Then we're back to square one."
**What do you do in the meeting?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep every check manual and ask for more operations staff"

prompt.text: Finance rejects the hiring request. The Head of Operations says the backlog is already 270 new supplier registrations after one week of the new process.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep every check and change the promise from 24 to 72 hours"

prompt.text: The Head of Sales refuses to sign: "72 hours means we lose customers to competitors." The CEO asks you for a recommendation by Friday.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Launch for one city first and decide later"

prompt.text: The Jaipur launch works, but the other cities are still on email and spreadsheets, and their backlog doubled because the best operations staff moved to the pilot.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior BA drafted these. **Name the most serious problems, worst first, and why each would cause trouble later.** Then rewrite one requirement properly.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: The system should be fast and user-friendly.
Every registration must be checked manually by the operations team.
Registrations under ₹50,000 with no issues are approved automatically.
As a reviewer, I want to see the registration's documents so that I can check them. Acceptance: documents are shown.
The system will send an SMS when a decision is made.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.

Write three user stories, with testable acceptance criteria, for the automatic route: a registration under ₹50,000 with no issues gets a decision without manual checks, and a random sample still goes to a person.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a project where stakeholders wanted conflicting things, and what you did.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
